newsitem.title: UK: European group plans coffee contract changes.
newsitem.headline: European group plans coffee contract changes.

text.p: The European Coffee Federation (ECF) said its contracts committee has proposed several changes to the European coffee contract established in 1956.
The changes being considered include a reduction in the weight franchise to 0.5 percent from 1.0 percent, the Brussels-based ECF said.
The weight franchise refers to the maximum acceptable loss in weight between the shipped and arrival weights.
Also being considered is a stipulation that bags used in shipping coffee must comply with the legal requirements for food packaging materials and waste management in the country of destination.
A new contract, namely the European Delivery Contract for Coffee, will be proposed by the committee.
The contract, which will cater for coffee in bags and in bulk, is intended to cover sales for future delivery at a European location.
"It is felt that this will fill a gap in current trading methods," the ECF said.
The other current contracts under review are the European Contract for Spot Coffee which will cover coffee in bags and in bulk as well as the European Contract for Coffee in Bulk.
The ECF annual meeting on June 3 is expected to consider and adopt the changes.
